# NOSOCOMIAL PNEUMONIA WITH ENTEROBACTERALES

# Citrobacter freundii, Klebsiella aerogenes, or Enterobacter cloacae treatment

These organisms are Amp C inducers and can develop resistance to certain beta-lactams (e.g., ceftriaxone) despite reported susceptibility or lack of resistance genes on rapid diagnostic panels

Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h R for 7 days

< OR >

Ertapenem 1 gm IV q24h R,O for 7 days

*Local guidance (Omaha CDSS, Inpatient):*
Meropenem 500 mg IV q6h [R,O] for 7 days

---

# Other Enterobacterales (E. coli, K. pneumoniae, P. mirabilis, etc.) treatment

# Ceftriaxone - susceptible or ESBL gene (CTX-M) not-detected

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h M for 7 days

# Ceftriaxone - resistance or ESBL gene (CTX-M) detected

Ertapenem 1 gm IV q24h R,O for 7 days

If critically ill:

Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h R,O for 7 days

---

References:

- Kalil AC et al. Clin Infect Dis 2016. 63:1
- Tamma PD. Clin Infect Dis. 2024 Aug 7:ciae403. doi: 10.1093/cid/ciae403
